newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 26.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Seoul University has become one of the major institutions to training to pass professional examinations.
- Apartment sales to be liberalised from January 1997, excluding flats in Seoul, Pusan, Taeju and Kwangju.
- Major companies are expected to have sweeping cuts in personnel, according to an industry insider. Five of South Korea's largest groups to cut about from 30 to 100 employees each.
- The United States has demanded a cut in prices of South Korean international telephone tolls.
- Among OECD members, South Korea is at the tail-end in terms of education investment, but Korean middle school students top the field in mathematics and science.
- The South Korean department store business has seen the lowest ever sales growth in nearly two decades.
